mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% over the prior quarter reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in a consecutive monthly pattern for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day forward returns despite sustained high FEDFUNDS, or the 60-day return exceeds the 20-day return by less than 5% in a statistically significant test.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum measured by PAYEMS above 160,000 monthly suggests labor market strength that supports corporate earnings growth and drives S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward return is negative when PAYEMS > 160,000 but UNRATE is above 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (GDPC1) by more than 10% in a month indicates weakening demand, which typically precedes a sharp decline in equity valuations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by more than 10% in a single month
failure_condition: GDPC1 declines >10% but S&P 500 posts a positive 5-day forward return with a p-value < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in the Industrial Production index above 105 (from 103) suggests supply-side expansion that can outpace demand, pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 60 days as valuations adjust.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 105 for 4 consecutive months with S&P 500 60-day forward return positive and statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: When the Unemployment Rate falls below 4.5% for three consecutive months, it signals labor market resilience that reduces policy uncertainty and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: UNRATE remains above 4.5% for 6 months while S&P 500 20-day forward returns are flat or negative.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in both employment (PAYEMS > 180,000) and housing starts (HOUST > 1,500) creates dual momentum that amplifies earnings and growth expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero when both PAYEMS > 180,000 and HOUST > 1,500 simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL below 320) during a Fed policy pause suggests deflationary pressure that tends to support risk assets and produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 320 in a month when FEDFUNDS is held constant
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL remains above 320 for 3 months while S&P 500 60-day returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: When the supply gauge RSAFS exceeds 750,000 for two consecutive months, it indicates robust manufacturing activity that can outpace consumer demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days as valuations adjust.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises above 750,000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: RSAFS > 750,000 for 2 months but S&P 500 5-day forward return is positive.
